cross_batch_observations: PF10 2.1: none of the 14 pages contains the stem TypeSafe or any instruction to report a TypeSafe reading. The only model/reasoning text in the batch is the T2 handoff-content exclusion ('model/reasoning/configuration instructions ... in a runnable handoff'), present once in each of the 9 CF pages. No T1 or T3 sentence exists in W1, so no page conflicts with 2.1, but no page implements the TypeSafe-reading report beside the handoff either. Whether these prompts must carry one is for the run to decide.

IA-10, IA-20, IA-30, IA-40 and IA-50 have no T2 sentence: their handoff contracts omit the explicit 'model/reasoning/configuration instructions' exclusion that every CF page carries. They do carry the D23-B enumerated-content wording ('The block names the exact destination prompt ... and, only for a condition those artifacts do not already record, the minimum context it needs.'), which already keeps model guidance out of the block. This is a wording-parity difference between the CF and IA families, not a conflict.

F05: in CF-C-30, CF-E-30 and IA-30, the sentence 'Write it page-ready and self-contained: one H2 heading with the next continuous number and a descriptive title, ...' says 'number' without the literal 'PF10' or 'addendum', so the brief's literal C rule leaves it out of c_quotes. It agrees with the N3 sentence on the same pages. The same sentence holds the only 'recommendations' match on those pages, classed T6 (an addendum content category).

F05: no N1 (universal 'no agent numbers') sentence appears anywhere in W1. IA-10's 'Never edit PF10 or allocate PF10 numbering.' is an imperative addressed to IA-10's own agent, and IA-10 is not one of the six producers, so it is classed N2 (a permitted exception). CF-PO-10's 'do not allocate or require a PF30 number' concerns PF30, not PF10 or an addendum, so it is outside C and unrelated to F05.

unresolved_questions: Taxonomy gap: some sentences forbid only model- or configuration-based routing and gating, not guidance. Examples are PE 'Do not create model, strength, reasoning-level, eligibility, suitability, account-availability, Analyzer, or configuration-based routing requirements.' and PE '...do not introduce a new assessment stage, alternate selection route, or configuration-based gate.' None of T1–T6 fits these exactly. I classed them as T5, the nearest class that does not forbid guidance, because PF10 2.1 says the reading is no gate, so they look consistent with it. Please confirm or reclassify.

PE 'Scan the complete authored bodies, templates, examples, and cross-references for obsolete external-storage identifiers and prohibited assessment or configuration routing.' could mean either 'prohibited (model) assessment' or 'prohibited assessment-routing'. I classed it as T1 to be conservative. If the second reading is intended, it belongs with the T5 routing-only group above.

PE N1 vs scoped: 'Preparing a standalone PF10 addendum does not authorize live PF10 inspection, numbering, ...' is classed N1 because it is universal on its face. If the coordinator reads it as limited to the PE's own prompt-maintenance task, it would be N2-like (PE is not a producer).

PE 'Outside GCFPE it does not allocate canon numbering, and Nathan pastes it into PF10 and allocates its number; for GCFPE the producer numbers it at creation...' combines N4 (outside GCFPE) and N3 (GCFPE). I classed it as N3 because the GCFPE clause is the one that governs here.
